A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DAS research, with matching authors, methodology and experimental suite. All 24 pages of v1 and 28 pages of v3, including appendices, equations, tables and figures, support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original LDS experiments on CIFAR, CelebA and ArtBench, acceleration ablations, sensitivity analyses and counterfactual image examples.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds quantitative counterfactual results, output-function diagnostics and further regularization analyses.

M1.justification: The noise-predictor output, linearization, Newton approximation, DAS formulas and acceleration techniques remain unchanged in Equations 9–18 and Algorithm 1. v3's identification of the existing curvature approximation as generalized Gauss–Newton documents the method without changing its procedure.

E1.justification: The dataset suite remains CIFAR-2, CIFAR-10, CelebA, ArtBench-2 and ArtBench-5, with the same image-generation attribution tasks and represented populations. The additional counterfactual, output-function and regularization diagnostics operate within this retained coverage.

E2.justification: TRAK joins D-TRAK and random deletion as comparators against DAS in the counterfactual experiment in Section 5.6 and Figure 9. v1's corresponding comparison used only D-TRAK and random deletion. Comparator membership in the main LDS tables remains unchanged.

E3.justification: v3 adds quantitative counterfactual evaluation over 60 generated images using pixel L2 distance and CLIP cosine similarity. It also introduces a separate random-deletion experiment correlating image differences with loss and noise-predictor differences. These substantially extend the evaluation design; the original LDS splits, model configurations and training recipes remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Regularization sensitivity expands from CIFAR-2 to four additional retained datasets in Figures 5–8. Sections 5.4 and 5.6 add output-function diagnostics and quantitative counterfactual analysis, including illustrative failure cases for loss differences. Earlier normalization, timestep, projection, checkpoint, up-block and candidate-set analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Figure 9 adds boxplots summarizing medians and variability across counterfactual image pairs. Existing LDS uncertainty reporting remains. Appendix E.2 also makes the one-versus-three training-seed policy consistent with the exceptions already stated in v1's main text; this does not establish an increase in repeated runs.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes DAS's CIFAR-10 generation LDS from 13.24 to 15.24 at 10 timesteps and from 18.99 to 23.69 at 100 timesteps, without a stated setting change. New results include counterfactual image-distance statistics, additional regularization curves and correlations of 0.257 for loss differences versus 0.485 for noise-predictor differences. Most existing table entries remain unchanged. The new CLIP medians have conflicting dataset assignments between the prose and Figure 9.

T1.justification: v3 adds a claimed KL/cross-entropy decomposition to Equation 8; v1 stops at the difference of two KL divergences. This is a localized mathematical addition, while the DAS derivations and appendix proofs remain unchanged. The added equality omits a generally nonzero term involving the log of the retrained distribution and therefore is not a general KL identity.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: limitations of loss-based attribution, theoretically derived DAS, computational acceleration and state-of-the-art LDS performance. The additional experiments support these existing claims without redefining the contribution.

C2.justification: v3 replaces the tentative explanation that large regularization is needed because of missing kernel normalization with a generalized Gauss–Newton, curvature and damping explanation. It also interprets the new toy results as showing that loss can reflect convergence while missing image-content changes. The stated resource, additivity and image-only limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-access link in the abstract and explicitly identifies the existing curvature approximation as generalized Gauss–Newton. The detailed dataset construction, model hyperparameters, optimizers and training schedules from v1 Appendix F.1 are retained in v3 Appendix E.1.

R1.justification: v3 adds discussion of DataInf, Brokman et al.'s training-monitoring method and concurrent K-FAC influence-function work, plus citations concerning LDS limitations and damping. Bourtoule et al. and Jacot et al. are removed from the references. The overall positioning around post-hoc diffusion attribution remains stable.

P1.justification: Related work moves from Appendix A to Section 2. The introduction, preliminaries, method motivation and acceleration discussion undergo extensive rewriting and condensation. Experiments are reorganized into separate output-function, LDS and counterfactual subsections, and applications move to Appendix I. Affiliations are corrected and acknowledgments added.

P2.justification: v3 adds seven figures covering regularization sweeps, counterfactual boxplots, correlation scatterplots and image pairs. Existing Figures 2–4 are relocated, and CelebA Table 3 moves into the appendix. Figure 1 is cropped/resized and recaptioned, while Tables 1 and 2 are grouped together.

improvement.justification: v3's quantitative counterfactual tests and output-function diagnostics strengthen validation beyond v1's LDS results and qualitative examples; broader sensitivity analysis and a code-access pointer also help. However, the new Equation 8 introduces an invalid equality into the central theoretical rationale, and Figure 9 conflicts with the prose's CLIP dataset assignments. These empirical gains coexist with theoretical and reporting harms, preventing a confident judgment of the net overall quality change.
